A dashboard of the data at this point; double-click to open it.

Connect any table. The dashboard starts with an automatic layout from the data's profile and column roles (the target, a card per column, correlations); add, remove and arrange widgets, and click a bar to filter every widget. The layout and filters are saved in the node; the data is read again, never saved in the graph.

None: the node ends a branch of the graph.

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dashboard_spec | `dashboard_spec` | Text | (empty) |   | The run | Dashboard layout (set in the Dashboard window) |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.
